_comment: Bible designer, axis 2 of 5 (story/designer/INTERVIEW.md): the kinds of things the book has. Each kind the author names becomes a table, in their word. Ask only what the premise makes plausible; a war history has no spells and a romance rarely has a supply chain. DECODER SAFETY: comment keys at this TOP LEVEL ONLY.
goal: Name the kinds of things the book keeps track of, one table per kind, in the author's words.

questions.ask: Who does the book follow? Is anyone more than one person — a family, a crew, an army, a faction?
questions.why: People go on the Characters table every bible already has. A group that acts as one (an army, a guild) is a table of its own.
questions.listenFor: the cast, and any group the author talks about as a single actor

questions.ask: Are there groups people belong to or answer to?
questions.why: Who answers to whom often changes over a book, and it is one of the first things a draft gets wrong.
questions.listenFor: factions, houses, guilds, units, parties, churches, companies

questions.ask: Are there things that matter enough to keep — objects, gear, documents, technology?
questions.why: A thing with rules or an owner is something a reader will check.
questions.listenFor: items with stated behaviour, items that change hands, inventions

questions.ask: Can people have or learn abilities — skills, powers, techniques, tactics?
questions.why: Abilities usually have a cost and a rank, which become columns.
questions.listenFor: skills, spells, classes, trades, tactics, training

questions.ask: Do any places have rules of their own?
questions.why: Places go on the Locations table. A place with its own rule (a floor, a front, a district) needs that rule where the model will see it.
questions.listenFor: levels, zones, fronts, cities with laws, worlds

questions.ask: Is there a system with its own rules — magic, a game interface, a technology, a law, a supply chain?
questions.why: A system's rules become World Rules rows, written as mechanism, cost and limit in the arc axis.
questions.listenFor: anything the author describes as working a certain way every time

doneWhen: Every kind the author named has a table name in their words, and you have said which go on the existing Characters, Locations, World Rules or Glossary tables.
